To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the picture-sort administration of a standard food frequency questionnaire was the best of the three instruments tested in this population, but the meal pattern-based instrument had the lowest correlation with the 24-hour recalls.

the picture-sort and the meal-based food frequency questionnaires were more accurate than the standard food frequency questionnaire in assessing dietary intake of low SES, elderly, multi-ethnic population.
The MPQ tended to have higher intakes than the FFQ and the PSFFQ; the PSFFQ had the highest correlations for women; and the FFQ had the highest correlation for men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a dietary assessment instrument for older adults of low socio-economic background.
developing a dietary assessment method for older, low SES, African American, Native and white adults, which is sensitive to the unique challenges faced by these populations.
the development of dietary assessment instruments for use with older adults who are members of racial/ethnic minority groups and who have low socioeconomic status.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MPQ was not as accurate as the PSFFQ and FFQ, but the PSFFQ may be a useful alternative for older adults who are unable to respond to standard FFQs.
the PSFFQ is more valid in women and the FFQ is more valid for men.
the MPQ overestimates intake, the PSFFG is more valid for women and the FFQ is more valid for men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MPQ is not recommended for use in the elderly, especially in low SES populations.
the FFQ was more reliable than the PSFFQ or the MPQ, but the PSFFQ had better validity for women and the MPQ was more reliable for men.
the FFQ and MPQ are comparable to the 24-hour recalls for assessing dietary intake of older, low SES adults.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary assessments should be conducted using multiple methods to obtain the most accurate information on dietary intake.
the MPQ is a promising tool for dietary assessment in this population.
dietary assessment instruments must be adapted to the population being studied.
